correctness.rationale: Classical planar Cheeger equation plus exact support-halfspace erosion and Steiner formulas prove the upper branch and threshold. Near the join, the polygonal inner-parallel area A-Ps+Cs^2 gives the analytic lower branch. Direct Taylor/implicit differentiation yields h double-prime right-minus-left=8 pi^2(C-pi)/(P+2sqrt(pi A))^3. Strict convexity of tan supplies the sharp equiangular bound. Algebra was independently checked symbolically and in high precision by the embedded script; all limits are proved, not inferred from simulations.

value.rationale: A naturally normalized, sharp second-order Cheeger response singularity measures the sum of polygonal half-angle cotangents for all convex polygons, even if their original Cheeger sets are irregular. A universal exact self-Cheeger cutoff identifies where a scalar global shape functional ceases to retain most shape data, while the cusp recovers the corner invariant and has a sharp equiangular equality criterion. It is not merely a numerical value or a renamed known inequality.
